1.tell: Set pairs two special cases (no solution / infinitely many) with two throwaway roots x=+-1; on a hard item the +-1 pair reads as the apparent-but-extraneous roots, so the designed answer is the special case, and 'no solution' is the more common payoff for an extraneous-root radical/rational item.

2.tell: 9 is the hub: 3 = sqrt(9) (forgot to square), 10 = 9+1 (off-by-one). 37 is unrelated debris. Parent = 9.

3.tell: 3 is the hub: 6 = 2x3 (doubled), 0 = degenerate slip. 4 is filler.

4.tell: Perfectly symmetric {+-2, +-3} - no structural tell at all. Guessed the small positive integer, which is the more common designed value in a sign-trap set.

5.tell: 200 sits at the centre of the manufactured family: 100 = half, 400 = double, 300 = one step off. A halving AND a doubling both pointing at the same value marks it as the parent.

6.tell: 6 is the hub: 3 = 6/2, 2 = 6/3, 9 = 1.5x6. Every other option is one arithmetic slip away from 6, and none of them are derivable from each other as cleanly.

7.tell: Strongest structural cue in the set: -4 and 2/3 are a plausible pair of roots and -10/3 is exactly their sum (-4 + 2/3). 0 is the degenerate filler. When the sum of two other options appears as a fourth, the question is asking for that sum.

8.tell: 6 is the composite of the rest (2x3, and 1,2,3 are its divisors); the small ints are partial-credit stopping points.

9.tell: -11 is a pure sign flip, which nominates 11 as the parent; 7 and 3 are unrelated fillers. Took the positive member of the flip pair.

12.tell: Same shape as item 7: 7 = 3+4, i.e. the sum of two other options is present, which usually means the stem asks for the combined quantity while 3 and 4 are the individual parts.

13.tell: All four are built from {3,7,2}: 7/2 shares its numerator with 7/3 and its denominator with 3/2, and 3/7 is its cross-swap. 7/2 is the one-swap hub of the family.

14.tell: 6 and 3 are the clean designed pair (3 = 6/2); 13/3 is a classic by-product decimal/fraction of a dropped term and 19 is unrelated debris. Clean small integer over odd fraction.

15.tell: No derivational relation among -5, 4, 1, -2. Guessed the clean positive integer.

17.tell: Only item where content survived redaction. A 12% annual decay written for m months is 8000(0.88)^(m/12); B inverts the exponent (12m), C substitutes an eyeballed monthly rate 0.99, D uses the decay amount 0.12 as the base. A is the only structurally correct exponential and the other three are its three standard mutations.

18.tell: 9 is the hub: 3 = sqrt(9), 36 = 4x9, 4 = the multiplier left over. Both a square-root slip and a factor-of-4 slip point back at 9.

19.tell: 5 is bracketed by 4 and 6, the two classic off-by-one slips; 21 is unrelated debris. The centre of a consecutive triple is the parent.

20.tell: 22/23 is an off-by-one pair and 45 = 22+23 is manufactured from it, so the answer is one of the pair; 9 is filler. Took the larger, since the common slip is failing to add the final unit.

22.tell: Two sign pairs {+-7, +-1}; the set is closed under negation so nothing is a by-product of anything. Guessed the larger positive.

23.tell: Two sign pairs {+-7, +-13}, closed under negation - no tell. Guessed the larger positive.
